centroid 2: every path either passes through 2 (thick: 1–2–5–7) or stays inside one piece

Centroid decomposition (点分治) answers questions about all paths of a tree. Take the centroid c (第9章): every path either passes through c, or lies completely inside one of the pieces left after removing c. Count the paths through c, then recurse into each piece with its own centroid.

Each piece has at most half the nodes, so the recursion is only O(log n) deep and every node is handled O(log n) times. If paths through c take O(size) (or O(size log size)), the whole run is O(n log n) (or O(n log² n)).

Is there a path of length exactly k (P3806)? At centroid c, collect each piece's distances; a distance d pairs with an earlier piece's k − d. Pieces are added one at a time so both ends never come from the same piece.
Clear only the entries you set, not the whole array.

Measure each piece's size afresh (pieceSize) before searching it for a centroid: sizes left over from an earlier search were measured from a different root. Mark the centroid removed before collecting, or paths will run back through it.
Keep the heavy child, re-add light subtrees.

DSU on tree (树上启发式合并 , small-to-large) answers a question for every subtree, like "how many colours appear in the subtree of u". Visit the light children first and throw their data away; visit the heavy child last and keep its data; then add u and the light subtrees again on top.

A node is re-added only when it sits in a light subtree of some ancestor, and there are at most log n light edges above it (第9章). So every node is added O(log n) times: O(n log n) total, with a single global count array.
Colours 1 2 1 2 3 on nodes 1–5: subtree of 2 is {2, 4, 5} with colours 2, 2, 3: two colours. Subtree of 1 has all three (U41492, CF600E asks for the most frequent colour instead).
The pattern "keep the biggest, merge the small ones into it" also works for sets and maps: merging small into large gives O(n log n) insertions (永无乡 P3224 in 第4章).
Key nodes + LCAs by DFS order and a stack.

A virtual tree (虚树) shrinks the tree to just the k key nodes of a query plus the LCAs between them (at most 2k nodes). Sort the key nodes by DFS order; the needed LCAs are those of adjacent pairs. Build it with a stack along the rightmost path, then run a tree DP on the small tree.

With many queries whose key nodes add up to K, each query costs O(k log n) instead of O(n): total O(K log n). Edges of the virtual tree stand for whole paths, so store what the DP needs about the path (here: its cheapest edge).

消耗战(P2495): cut edges so no key node can reach node 1, at least total cost. For a node u of the virtual tree, either cut the cheapest edge between the root and u (mn[u]), or solve each child separately; a key node must be cut above itself. Clearing vt[] and key_[] inside the DP keeps each query O(k).

The sentinel node 1 must always be on the stack bottom, and the stack loop compares depths of the second-to-top node with the LCA. Getting the order of those two checks wrong silently builds a wrong tree.
